belief: My church's rules are the same as God's love.
origins: Where rules about dress, music, entertainment, or conduct are taught as the heart of faith, breaking one can feel like losing God’s favor. We confuse a community’s customs with God’s character and cannot tell where the church ends and God begins.
teaches: Jesus said, “You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.” Paul writes, “It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not be encumbered once more by a yoke of slavery.” He also warns against human rules, “Do not handle, do not taste, do not touch!” which “are of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.” And “neither death nor life… nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.” God’s love is not earned by keeping a church’s rules. Real obedience flows from that love.
self_statements: If I break a rule, God is angry.
The rules are what God wants.
I am only loved if I conform.
If they disapprove, God does too.
I am safe when I follow every rule.
errors: Believing I am either obedient to all rules or rejected.
Assuming the church speaks for God in everything.
Feeling guilty and concluding that God is displeased.
questions: Which rules are in Scripture, and which are customs?
What does Scripture say is the heart of God’s will?
How do I feel when I break a church rule?
Does God’s love depend on my keeping those rules?
Who in my church lives in freedom and love?
What would help me sort out the difference?
truth: God’s love is not the same as my church’s rules. I can honor godly leaders and clear Scripture while recognizing human customs. Nothing can separate me from the love of God in Christ.
hw_truths: Human traditions are not God’s commands.
Nothing can separate me from God’s love.
I can honor leaders and test teaching.
I obey out of love, not fear.
log: Each week, note one act of obedience out of love, not fear.
actions: Write which are Scripture and which are custom.
prayer: Father, You love me apart from rules. Help me tell Your commands from human customs, obey out of love, and rest in Your grace. Amen.
hw_questions: What is the heart of God’s will?
How do I feel when I break a rule?
Does God’s love depend on them?
What helps me sort it out?
